problems: empire-of-haiti has no dossier file: its seven shapes are reviewed in haiti.json (cliopatria_names Haiti and Empire of Haiti). colours.json gives haiti, empire-of-haiti and republic-of-haiti three colours; they are one state and should share one. haiti.json ends in 1935 (row boundary, dissolve is bookkeeping) and names republic-of-haiti (another part) as successor; that dossier should list haiti as predecessor.
republic-of-venezuela is kept separate from venezuela (1834-2024) although both carry Q717; the venezuela dossier should list republic-of-venezuela and gran-colombia as predecessors.

new-granada_1820 (1820-1821, 1.34 M km2 with 191,000 km2 in Brazil) is verdict wrong; gran-colombia (another part) should cover 1819-1821 or the Cliopatria hole stays empty. first-mexican-empire (another part) should say who held the land in 1821. dominican-republic (another part) should start in 1844, not 1846.

mexicans and republic-of-venezuela start in 1810, before Cliopatria's first shape (1811), and carry a new 1810 keyframe; haiti, new-granada, paraguay and republic-of-venezuela fill years Cliopatria leaves empty (haiti 1803-1804 and 1916-1935; new-granada 1816-1819 as a rump; paraguay 1870-1876; republic-of-venezuela 1810).

Occupation events follow the schema's 'roles reversed' rule: paraguay records its own conquests (counterparts empire-of-brazil, argentine-confederation) and the Allied occupation of Paraguay (counterpart empire-of-brazil, owner's side); haiti records the US occupation from the owner's side. The empire-of-brazil, argentine-confederation and united-states-of-america dossiers should carry the mirrors.
